description: PRD-104: Ephemeral Agents & Model Selection — Full research + design PRD. Study agent spawning patterns, model routing, cost optimization. Design contractor agent lifecycle and model-per-role strategy.

userStories.title: Research agent spawning and lifecycle patterns
userStories.description: As a researcher, I need to study how existing systems create and destroy temporary agents so that our contractor model is informed by prior art
acceptanceCriteria: Study Agent Zero's delegation model — how it spawns sub-agents, conversation sealing, cleanup
Study AutoGen's agent creation — dynamic agent instantiation, termination conditions
Study K8s Job lifecycle — create, run, complete, cleanup. TTL-after-finished pattern
Study serverless function lifecycle — cold start, warm pool, timeout, cleanup
Study CrewAI's agent definition — how roles/goals/backstory configure agent behavior
Comparison table: system, spawn time, lifecycle model, cleanup strategy, state persistence
Write to PRD section: '## 2. Prior Art: Agent Lifecycle Patterns'
Address PRD-100 Open Question #4: 'How fast can we spin up a contractor agent?'
userStories.notes: Key insight from PRD-100: contractors are mission-scoped, destroyed after. But their outputs (reports, board tasks, telemetry) persist. The question is whether they need a DB record (agents table row) or can be purely in-memory.

userStories.title: Research model routing and selection
userStories.description: As a researcher, I need to study model routing strategies so that our model-per-role design optimizes cost and quality
acceptanceCriteria: Study Martian model routing — how it selects models based on task characteristics
Study Unify.ai's model selection — quality/cost/speed optimization
Study OpenRouter's model metadata — what info is available for programmatic selection
Research model benchmarks by task type: reasoning (MMLU, ARC), coding (HumanEval, SWE-bench), writing (creative/technical), research (retrieval, synthesis)
Document cost tiers: cheap models (<$1/M tokens), mid ($1-10/M), premium (>$10/M) with quality tradeoffs
Write to PRD section: '## 3. Model Routing & Selection'
Include decision matrix: task_type × quality_requirement → model tier
Address PRD-100 Open Question #6: cost difference between routing strategies
userStories.notes: Automatos has 340 models via OpenRouter. config.py has LLM_MODEL as default. The model-per-role strategy should recommend models but allow user override. Don't build a dynamic routing engine — start with a static mapping that can evolve.

userStories.title: Design contractor agent lifecycle
userStories.description: As a platform architect, I need the contractor agent lifecycle designed end-to-end
acceptanceCriteria: Define lifecycle phases: request → configure → spawn → execute → report → cleanup
Define contractor configuration: role description, tools needed, model, context mode, memory scope (mission-only)
Define DB strategy: lightweight agents table row with is_contractor=true and mission_run_id FK, OR ephemeral (no DB record)
Recommend DB approach with rationale — consider: what if we need to query 'all contractors for run X'
Define cleanup: what happens when mission completes — mark inactive, remove from roster, archive config
Define what persists after cleanup: reports, board tasks, telemetry events, memory (none)
Write to PRD section: '## 4. Contractor Agent Lifecycle'
Include lifecycle state diagram
userStories.notes: The existing agents table has fields like: name, model, skill, personality, workspace_id. A contractor would need most of these but with a mission-scoped lifecycle. Adding is_contractor boolean + run_id FK is probably simplest. Read the agents model to decide.

userStories.title: Design model-per-role configuration
userStories.description: As a platform architect, I need model-per-role configuration designed so that users can optimize cost/quality per task type
acceptanceCriteria: Define role taxonomy: planner, researcher, writer, coder, reviewer, verifier, coordinator
Define default model mapping per role — sensible defaults from OpenRouter catalog
Define override hierarchy: platform defaults → workspace settings → mission config → task override
Define cost estimation — given a model mapping and task count, estimate mission cost before execution
Connect to orchestration_runs.config JSONB (PRD-101) — where model prefs are stored
Write to PRD section: '## 5. Model-Per-Role Configuration'
Include default mapping table with model IDs, costs, and rationale
Include cost estimation formula
userStories.notes: OpenRouter provides per-model pricing in its API. The cost estimation should use real pricing data. Start with 3 tiers: cheap (deepseek-chat), balanced (claude-sonnet), premium (claude-opus). User can customize per workspace.

userStories.title: Design AgentFactory integration for contractors
userStories.description: As a platform architect, I need to design how contractors use the existing AgentFactory without breaking it
acceptanceCriteria: Define how coordinator calls AgentFactory for contractors — new method or existing execute_with_prompt
Define contractor tool assignment — does coordinator specify tools or does tool_router handle it
Define contractor context — which ContextService mode, what sections, what's in the system prompt
Address: contractors have no personality, no long-term memory, no skills — how does ContextService handle this
Define contractor output capture — how results flow back to coordinator
Write to PRD section: '## 6. AgentFactory Integration'
Include code flow diagram showing coordinator → AgentFactory → LLM → output → coordinator
userStories.notes: AgentFactory.execute_with_prompt already handles the full tool loop. Contractors should use this same path. The key difference: contractors get mission-scoped context (goal, task description, prior task outputs) instead of personality-driven context. A new CONTRACTOR context mode in ContextService might be needed.

userStories.title: Write PRD-104 opening, synthesis, and conclusion
userStories.description: As a document author, I need to write the complete PRD-104 document
acceptanceCriteria: Create docs/PRDS/104-EPHEMERAL-AGENTS-MODEL-SELECTION.md
Header, Problem Statement, synthesis of US-001 through US-005
Design Decisions Made table
Risk Register (at least 5 risks)
Implementation Acceptance Criteria
Appendix: Contractor configuration schema (JSON example)
Appendix: Default model mapping table
Final review pass — cross-references to PRD-101, PRD-102 valid
PRD-104 complete and ready for peer review
userStories.notes: Follow PRD-100 style. This PRD is smaller scope than 101/102 — don't pad it. 6 stories instead of 8.
